clue.text: Cake lacking icing at first

indicators.note: what comes at first is the opening letter of the word it follows

blocks.note: poor means lacking, deficient
the opening letter of icing

explanation.surface: A plain cake that has no icing on top.
explanation.walkthrough: A poori is a small round of unleavened Indian bread, deep-fried; Chambers calls it a cake, which makes the definition fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Dictionaries describe this puffed, deep-fried Indian bread as a small flat cake of unleavened dough.

clue.text: Life on crisps affected fertility

indicators.note: something affected has been altered, so the letters are changed in order

blocks.note: the fodder, every letter used

explanation.surface: A diet of potato crisps damaged someone's ability to have children.
explanation.definitionFit: Prolificness is the quality of producing offspring abundantly, which is what fertility means.

clue.text: Nymph in rock poster?

blocks.note: ore is rock containing metal
a poster is an advertisement, an ad

explanation.surface: A wall poster of a nymph sitting on a rock.
explanation.walkthrough: An oread in Greek myth is a mountain nymph, which makes rock a fitting surface touch.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek mythology an oread is a nymph of mountains and hills.

clue.text: Shower one new pet with designer clothing

indicators.note: clothing means covering or dressing, so one name wraps round the other

blocks.note: the Roman numeral one
N is the abbreviation for new
Christian Dior, the French fashion designer
a cat is a common pet

explanation.surface: A pampered pet dressed in a designer outfit for a party.
explanation.walkthrough: Shower is one who shows, not a wash or a burst of rain.
explanation.definitionFit: An indicator is something that points out or shows a value or state, so literally a shower.

clue.text: Dallying in game with King missing lines

indicators.note: missing means going without, so the named letter is dropped from the game

blocks.note: a lawn game played with mallets and hoops
R for Rex, Latin for king
RY, short for railway: railway lines

explanation.surface: Someone plays a game without a king, as if dawdling over chess.
explanation.walkthrough: RY is the standard abbreviation for railway, so lines here means railway lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Coquetry is flirtatious behaviour, and dallying in its older sense means flirting or toying amorously.

clue.text: Tea chest turned up in yoga centre

indicators.note: in a down answer, turned up means read from bottom to top

blocks.note: cha is slang for tea
an ark is a chest or box, as in the Ark of the Covenant

explanation.surface: A tea chest is upended in the middle of a yoga studio.
explanation.walkthrough: Yoga centre looks like a studio; it means one of the body's energy centres in yoga.
explanation.definitionFit: In yoga and Hindu tradition a chakra is one of the body's points of spiritual energy, called centres.

clue.text: Bog paper hiding naughty mag

indicators.note: naughty means misbehaving, so the letters are out of line
hiding something means holding it out of sight within

blocks.note: a quire is a set of 24 or 25 sheets of paper
the fodder, every letter used

explanation.surface: Someone hides a smutty magazine inside the toilet paper.
explanation.walkthrough: Bog is British slang for toilet, which colours the surface with bog paper; here it is the definition, marshy ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A quagmire is a soft, wet area of land that gives way underfoot, the same as a bog.

clue.text: John briefly upset George perhaps

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the word loses its last letter
in a down answer, upset means tipped over and read upwards

blocks.note: john is slang for a toilet

explanation.surface: A man called John is upset with his friend George.
explanation.walkthrough: John looks like a man's name; it is the slang word for a lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: George Eliot was the pen name of the novelist Mary Ann Evans, so George is an example bearing that surname.

clue.text: Check about test case finally and investigate again

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other
finally points to the last letter of the word before it

blocks.note: to rein in is to check
an exam is a test
the final letter of case

explanation.surface: A detective goes over a test case once more before reopening it.
explanation.walkthrough: Check looks like the definition, but it is a verb meaning restrain, holding the test inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To examine something a second time is to look into it anew, which is investigating it again.

clue.text: Movie star reads Metamorphosis and hams it up

indicators.note: a metamorphosis is a complete change of form, so the letters before it are reshaped

blocks.note: the fodder, every letter used

explanation.surface: A film actor reads Kafka's story aloud on stage and plays it far too big.
explanation.walkthrough: Metamorphosis, capitalised, looks like the title of Kafka's story; here it is just the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To ham it up is to act with exaggerated theatricality, which is exactly what overdramatising means.

clue.text: Building close to New Forest is one used for smoking

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so its last letter is kept

blocks.note: a church is a building
the final letter of new
the Forest of Arden in Warwickshire, setting of As You Like It

explanation.surface: A building near the New Forest where people go to smoke.
explanation.walkthrough: The New Forest is a real area of southern England, so the eye reads New Forest as one name; split it.
explanation.definitionFit: A churchwarden is a long-stemmed clay tobacco pipe, something used for smoking.

clue.text: Fashionable style of art with peculiar lack of taste

blocks.note: in fashion
Art Deco, the 1920s–30s design style
rum is British slang for odd or peculiar

explanation.surface: A trendy art style is mocked for its strange tastelessness.
explanation.walkthrough: Rum here is the British adjective meaning strange, not the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Indecorum is a breach of propriety or good form, a failure of taste in behaviour.

clue.text: Romeo cutting facial hair in pan

indicators.note: a thing cutting into another sits inside it, splitting it in two

blocks.note: tash is British slang for a moustache
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A shaving scene: Romeo trims his facial hair over a pan of water.
explanation.walkthrough: Pan is the verb, to criticise harshly, not the cooking vessel; a tash is a British moustache.
explanation.definitionFit: To trash a film or play is to slate it severely, the same as panning it in a review.

clue.text: Clowns one spots touring island

indicators.note: touring means going around, so one word travels round another

blocks.note: the Roman numeral one
spots are dots
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A circus act: one clown with spotty costume goes on tour round an island.
explanation.walkthrough: I is followed by DOTS wrapped round the second I.
explanation.definitionFit: Clowns in the sense of fools: people who behave stupidly, which is what idiots are.

clue.text: Revolutionary man is under cover briefly

indicators.note: in a down answer, a thing under another is written below it
briefly means cut short, so the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: to insure is to provide cover
a gent is a man

explanation.surface: A rebel is a man working briefly undercover.
explanation.walkthrough: Under cover reads as undercover; split it, and the man goes below the shortened INSURE.
explanation.definitionFit: An insurgent is a rebel taking up arms against authority, a revolutionary.

clue.text: More difficult to pull in lace underwear ultimately

indicators.note: in places one word inside the other
ultimately points to the very end of the word it follows

blocks.note: to lace is to tie
to rick is to wrench or pull a muscle
the final letter of underwear

explanation.surface: Getting laced underwear on is a harder pull than you would think.
explanation.walkthrough: Pull is the injury sense, as in pulling a muscle, and lace is a verb, to fasten.
explanation.definitionFit: Trickier is the comparative of tricky, meaning harder to handle or more difficult.

clue.text: Diamond found in C&A party

blocks.note: C is the chemical symbol for carbon
taken as written
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A diamond turns up at a party held by C&A, the British clothing chain.
explanation.walkthrough: C&A looks like the high-street store; read C as the symbol it stands for, expanded to CARBON, then A and DO.
explanation.definitionFit: Carbonado is a black, porous variety of diamond used industrially for drilling.

clue.text: Stormy romance with leader of America being filmed

indicators.note: stormy means turbulent, so the letters are thrown about
the leader of a word is the letter at its front

blocks.note: the main fodder
the opening letter of America

explanation.surface: A turbulent love affair with a US president being captured by the cameras.
explanation.definitionFit: On camera means in front of a recording camera, so being filmed or televised.

clue.text: Accessory in Tamworth criminal group on edge

indicators.note: in an across answer, one thing placed on another comes after it

blocks.note: to nose or edge forward, to move ahead slowly
a ring is a gang of criminals

explanation.surface: A crime gang in the Staffordshire town of Tamworth is getting nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: Tamworth is a town but also a breed of pig; a pig wears a ring through its snout, so it is an accessory of the Tamworth.
explanation.definitionFit: Farmers fit a metal ring through a pig's snout to stop it rooting, an item a Tamworth pig wears.

clue.text: Awkward delivery bowled on repeat, endlessly

indicators.note: endlessly means without an end, so the last letter is cut off

blocks.note: B is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for bowled
re means on or about
an echo is a repeat of a sound

explanation.surface: A cricket commentator replays a clumsy ball over and over.
explanation.walkthrough: Delivery suggests a cricket ball, given 'bowled'; it is a birth, and a breech birth is one where the baby comes feet or bottom first.
explanation.definitionFit: A breech birth, with the baby positioned bottom first, is a difficult childbirth, so an awkward delivery.

clue.text: Book with twenty per cent off by journalist: good for the consumer!

indicators.note: a fifth taken off a five-letter word means dropping one of its letters
by means next to, so the two pieces sit side by side

blocks.note: ED, short for editor
the Bible, the Book

explanation.surface: A book discounted by a fifth, as a journalist tells shoppers: a good deal for the consumer.
explanation.walkthrough: BIBLE has five letters, so twenty per cent is one letter, its first B.
explanation.definitionFit: Edible means safe to eat, so something good for whoever consumes it.

clue.text: Hint of rum in double in sailors' bar

indicators.note: a hint of something is just a trace, its opening letter
in places one item inside the other

blocks.note: the spit of someone is their double, as in spitting image
the opening letter of rum

explanation.surface: A dash of rum in a double measure at the bar where sailors drink.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes inside SPIT. Sailors' bar looks like a pub; it is a spar on a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprit is a small spar running diagonally to support a sail, a bar used by sailors.

clue.text: Screw up in audition for Superman?

indicators.note: an audition is a hearing, so the word is judged by its sound

blocks.note: to screw up a bolt is to make it tighter

explanation.surface: An actor blows the screen test for the part of Superman.
explanation.walkthrough: Screw up suggests a botch; it means tighten. Superman? is a definition by example, with the question mark flagging it.
explanation.definitionFit: A titan is a person of superhuman strength or stature, after the giant gods of Greek myth.

clue.text: Dan Dare adaptation receiving award for stars

indicators.note: an adaptation reworks something into a new form
receiving means taking something in, so one piece holds the other

blocks.note: the fodder, every letter used
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A screen version of the space hero Dan Dare wins a prize for its stars.
explanation.walkthrough: Dan Dare is a British comic-strip space pilot from the Eagle comic, so stars fits the surface neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: Andromeda is a northern constellation, a named group of stars.

clue.text: Boredom at night in Paris cut short

indicators.note: cut short means trimmed at the end, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: en nuit is French for at night

explanation.surface: A night out in Paris ends early because it is so dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is a French loanword for listless weariness and dissatisfaction, which is boredom.

clue.text: Silly to pamper cats and dogs inside?

indicators.note: inside means placed within, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: to featherbed is to cosset or pamper
raining cats and dogs means raining heavily

explanation.surface: Fussing over pets indoors might strike some people as daft.
explanation.walkthrough: RAIN goes inside FEATHERBED, between B and ED. Cats and dogs looks like the pets being pampered; it stands for heavy rain.
explanation.definitionFit: Featherbrained describes a scatty, foolish person, someone silly or empty-headed.

clue.text: Learned about character in part of history

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

blocks.note: a sage is wise and learned
tone is character or quality, as in the tone of a place

explanation.surface: A scholar writes about a character from a period of the past.
explanation.walkthrough: Learned is the adjective (two syllables), not the past tense of learn.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stone Age is the prehistoric era of stone tools, a period of human history.

clue.text: Cricket sides drawing in India — it could bring tears to your eyes!

definitions.text: it could bring tears to your eyes!

indicators.note: drawing in means pulling something inside, so the sides enclose a letter

blocks.note: the on side is a half of a cricket field, here taken twice for sides
India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Two cricket teams playing out a draw in India is a heartbreaking result.
explanation.walkthrough: The on side (or leg side) is the half of a cricket field behind the batsman's legs; two of them make the sides.
explanation.definitionFit: Chopping an onion releases a sulphur compound that irritates the eyes and makes them water.
